Haptic music engineering vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume Music Haptics capability covers storefront language. Xcode, Core Haptics, and Connect actually separate haptic playback in the app from product-page copy:

  • Core Haptics & CHHapticEngine patterns — in-app code that maps song beats to Taptic Engine vibration. Controls timing, intensity, and device support. Does not generate Chinese listing text.
  • Music Haptics sync pipelines — engineering work for analyzing audio rhythm, routing playback to haptic output, and pairing with Accessibility Music Haptics settings. Separate from the zh-Hans description paragraph that explains feel-the-music value to buyers.
  • Device & song scope — your binary may support specific headphones, iPhone models, or track types. Listing copy should match what screenshots actually show — not promise universal Music Haptics for every song when your gallery only shows demo tracks.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of haptic music integration in the app.

Working Music Haptics flows in the binary and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other.
